ui.appOnly: This works in the installed app.
toast.loadFail: Your setup could not be read: {e}
lv.read.hint: Looks at files and git history, changes nothing.
lv.edit.hint: May change files in the folders and run the allowed commands. No commits.
lv.commit.hint: Also commits — nothing leaves your computer. Commits can be undone in the history.
lv.publish.hint: Also pushes, tags and creates releases on GitHub. Force-push is never allowed.

inbox.empty: When Claude has a question, needs an approval or is done, it shows up here — and as a notification.
todo.how: How Claude works on to-dos (all lists)
todo.howNone: No folder chosen yet — choose where Claude works on the items.
todo.empty: Link any Markdown file with checkboxes (- [ ] …), e.g. your TODO.md. You keep writing it as before; Claude works on the items.
todo.needDirs: First choose the folder Claude works in.
todo.prompt:
Do this item of my to-do list ({path}{where}):

{text}
todo.promptAll: Work through the open items of my to-do list {path} in order (higher up = more important). Don’t tick anything yourself; say at the end exactly which items are done.
todo.profileHint: Used for every list without its own folders and rights.
todo.extraPh: e.g. Note what you did in STATUS.md.
rt.sub: Claude works on them by itself — on schedule or by button
rt.empty: A routine is a standing task: what to do, where, with which rights and when. Start with a template.
rt.newHint: Pick a template — you can change everything afterwards.
rt.delAsk: Delete “{name}”? Its runs stay in the history.
sch.manual.hint: Starts only when you press Start.
sch.daily.hint: Runs while Agent Studio is open; a missed time is caught up when it opens.
sch.weekdays.hint: Monday to Friday; a missed time is caught up when Agent Studio opens.
sch.weekly.hint: Once a week; a missed time is caught up when Agent Studio opens.
sch.start.hint: Once every time Agent Studio opens.
sch.todo.hint: A minute after you last changed the list.
tpl.todo.desc: Every morning: open items of your linked list, results noted.
tpl.todo.prompt: Work through the open items of my to-do list {todo} in order (higher up = more important). Commit each item on its own. Say at the end which items are done and what is open.
tpl.bugs.desc: Looks for bugs and weak spots, changes nothing.
tpl.bugs.prompt: Look through the code in these folders for bugs, risky spots and things that don’t fit together. Change nothing. Report the most important findings with file and line, most serious first.
tpl.builds.desc: Are the last GitHub Actions runs green?
tpl.builds.prompt: Check for the repositories in these folders whether the latest GitHub Actions runs succeeded (gh run list). For failed ones say which job failed and why, in short.
tpl.week.desc: What changed this week, what is open.
tpl.week.prompt: Sum up what changed in these folders in the last 7 days (git log, changed files) and what is still open (TODO notes, open items). Short, as a list.
tpl.notes.desc: Turns the files of a folder into a Markdown summary.
tpl.notes.prompt: Read the notes and documents in this folder and write a clear study sheet as Lernzettel.md: the key terms, the most important facts and 5 questions to test myself. Keep the other files as they are.
tpl.deps.desc: Outdated packages and known problems — suggestions only.
tpl.deps.prompt: Check whether the dependencies in these folders (Cargo.toml, package.json …) are outdated or have known problems. Change nothing; suggest which updates are worth it and why.
hist.clearAsk: Remove all runs and their logs from the history? Runs with an open note in “Needs you” stay.
run.undoAsk: Take back the commits of this run? The files go back to how they were before the run; your own changes since stay.
det.none: Select a run, a routine or “How Claude works on to-dos” to see the details here.
det.chatPh: A question, a correction, the next step…
det.chatHint: Goes on in the same conversation, with the same rights.
ed.name: Name
ed.dirsHint: Claude starts in the first folder and may only work in these.

ed.web: May use the internet (search, open pages)
ed.planOnly: Plan only — say what would be done, change nothing
ed.limitHint: 0 = no limit. After the limit the run is stopped.
ed.rulesPh: One rule per line, e.g. Commit messages in German.
task.title: New task
task.whatPh: e.g. Fix the bug that the icon on the start page is blurry, and commit it.
limit.title: Daily limit
limit.ask: Claude has already worked {n} minutes today — your daily limit. Start anyway?
limit.reached: Daily limit reached — routines wait until tomorrow.
ctx.running: Claude is working — every step shows up in the run’s log.
cl.notFoundHint: Agent Studio uses Claude Code. Install it (claude.com/claude-code) or choose the program in Settings → Claude Code.
cl.signInHint: Sign in once with your Claude account — your browser opens. Agent Studio itself never sees or stores a password.
cl.programHint: The program that does the work. Found by itself (installer, npm, Homebrew or the Claude app) — or set its path.
cl.code: If a code is asked for: paste it here
cl.privacy: Routines, logs and history stay on this computer. What Claude reads in a run is sent to Claude to do the work.
ctl.rulesHint: Claude gets them in every run, one per line.
ctl.rulesPh:
Write commit messages in German.
Never push without asking.
Keep the changelog up to date.
ctl.limitHint: How long Claude may work per day. Routines wait after that; for your own tasks you are asked.
ctl.safetyHint: Whatever the rights: no force-push, no git reset --hard, no git clean, no sudo. Anything beyond a run’s rights is refused and comes to “Needs you” for approval. Only Agent Studio’s rights count — other Claude Code settings are not used in runs.
set.languageHint: The language of menus, dialogs — and of Claude’s answers.
set.autoHide: Auto-hide bars (they slide in at the screen edge)
set.doneNotesHint: Questions, approvals and problems always come there; finished runs are in the history anyway.
about.p1: Agent Studio is for building apps with AI: every project has its rights, tasks, sessions with Claude, commands and changes.
about.p2: It uses Claude Code with your own sign-in. Agent Studio keeps no keys or passwords; routines, logs and history stay on this computer.
about.p3: Part of the Studio apps. Unlike the others it needs the internet and a Claude account.
todo.doneLess: Show only the last {n} ticked items
todo.own: Own folders and rights for this list
todo.ownHint: This list uses its own settings below.
todo.ownOff: This list uses the settings for all lists. Turn on to give it its own folders and rights (e.g. one list per project).
ed.auto: Auto mode — don’t ask for every step
ed.autoHint: Off: only what the rights allow, everything else comes to you for approval.
ed.autoOn: Claude works on its own within the rights: any command, no question for each step. Claude Code checks every step and still refuses risky ones (e.g. sending data out) — those come to you. Beyond the rights nothing is allowed, never force-push.
todo.addGoHint: Adds the to-do and lets Claude work on it right away (Ctrl+Enter)
full.chatPh: Reply or tell Claude something new…
full.chatBusy: Claude is working – you can already type ahead…
full.chatFoot: Enter sends · / for commands · Shift+Enter for a new line · goes on in the same conversation, with the same rights
sl.clear: Start a new conversation (Claude forgets this one; same rights and folders)
sl.model: Choose the model for the next messages
sl.plan: Only plan the next step — Claude says what it would do and changes nothing
sl.compact: Summarise the conversation so far so it takes less room

sl.diff: Show the changes of this run
sl.full: Open or close the full view

sl.planSet: The next message is only planned.
sl.noSession: There is no conversation to summarise yet.
sl.costIs: This conversation has cost {c} so far.
sl.unknown: Unknown command /{name} — /help shows all. To send a text starting with /, write //.
sl.busy: Claude is still working — wait or stop it (/stop).
sl.helpIntro: Type / in the chat box: ↑/↓ choose, Tab or Enter take the command, Esc closes the list. Your own commands come from ~/.claude/commands and ~/.claude/skills and from .claude/ in the run's folders.
sl.noOwn: No own commands or skills found yet.

link.title: Tasks from other Studio apps
link.hint: Markdown, PDF, Data, Slides and Plan Studio can send a file or a selection with a task (“Send to Agent Studio”). It runs as a chat here; the answer and new files go back to the app. It is never allowed to commit, push or delete.
link.accept: Take tasks from other Studio apps
link.web: They may use the internet (when the app asks for it)
link.levelEdit: Change files in the file's folder
gpt.hint: Choose a ChatGPT model wherever you pick a model — for a chat, a routine, a task, or here as the standard. The work is done by OpenAI's Codex CLI (the codex program) with your ChatGPT account. Agent Studio sees and stores no password.
gpt.notFoundHint: Install it (e.g. npm install -g @openai/codex or brew install codex) or choose the program here.
gpt.signInHint: Sign in once with your ChatGPT account — your browser opens.
gpt.privacy: What ChatGPT reads in a run goes to OpenAI for processing.
gpt.rights: With ChatGPT, Codex's sandbox sets the limits: it may change files in the folders at most and can read files elsewhere too. Commits and pushes stay with you, even at higher rights. It doesn't know rules per command: "never delete" and the allowed commands are only told to the model, not enforced.
home.sub: Your apps — and what Claude is doing on them
home.emptyTitle: Build your first app with AI
home.empty: Make a new app — Claude sets it up for you — or add a folder you already work on. Every project has its own rights, tasks, commands and changes.
p.noSessions: No session yet — write above what Claude should build.
p.noTodoHint: Link a Markdown file with checkboxes (- [ ] …), e.g. TODO.md — Claude works through the items with this project's rights.
p.noCmds: No commands found — add one below (e.g. npm test).
p.openDirHint: Open the folder with the system's program
p.appsHint: Each app gets a project of its own with its own commands and changes — the rights of this folder are taken over.
p.commitNeedsLevel: The project needs at least the right "commit" for this (Setup).
p.folderHint: Claude starts here and the commands run here.
p.extraDirsHint: Folders Claude may use in this project too (e.g. a shared library).
p.rulesPh: e.g. "Keep the CHANGELOG up to date", "Test before every commit"
p.rulesHint: For every session in this project — on top of the rules for all.
p.shortHint: Up to three characters on the project's tile — leave empty for the initials of the name.
p.keyHint: Opens the project from anywhere. Click and press the keys (with Ctrl or Alt); Delete removes it, Esc cancels.
p.keyMenu: {k} already belongs to "{a}" — please pick another one (or change it in Settings under Shortcuts).
p.aboutPh: e.g. "Tauri app: Rust in src-tauri/, the UI is plain HTML/JS in ui/. Texts always in German and English."
p.aboutHint: Like a system prompt: in every session Claude is told which project it works on (name, version, kind, folders) — and this text.
p.removeAsk: Remove "{name}" from Agent Studio? The folder and its files stay as they are; the sessions stay in the history.
p.rightsHint: These rights count for every session, task and routine in this project. Reviews and questions always run with read rights only.
work.foot: Claude works in {dirs} — with the project's rights. Enter starts, Shift+Enter for a new line.
work.feature.ph: What should {name} be able to do?
work.feature.prompt:
Build this feature in {name}: {text}

First look at how the project is built and keep to its style. Test what you built (build and tests, as far as you may run them), and keep README and CHANGELOG up to date if there are any.
work.fix.hint: Find a bug and fix it
work.fix.ph: What doesn't work in {name}? (error message, steps …)
work.fix.prompt:
Fix this bug in {name}: {text}

Find the cause first (not just the symptom), fix it with a change as small as possible, and check with build and tests that it is gone and nothing else broke. If it fits, write a test that finds the bug in future.
work.test.prompt:
Write tests for {name}: {text}

Use the test tool the project already uses; test the behavior, not the implementation, edge cases too. Run the tests and say what they cover. If you find bugs, describe them instead of fixing them silently.
work.refactor.ph: What should be cleaned up in {name}?
work.refactor.prompt:
Clean up in {name}: {text}

The behavior stays exactly the same. Go in small steps, check each with build and tests, and say at the end what got simpler.
work.review.ph: What should Claude review in {name}? (e.g. "the last changes")
work.review.prompt:
Do a code review in {name}: {text}

Change nothing. Look for real bugs (wrong behavior, crashes, security holes, data loss) first, then for unclear and needless code. For each point give file and line, why it is a problem and how to fix it — the most important first.
work.release.hint: Version, changelog, tag — publishing only with approval
work.release.ph: Which version, what goes in? (e.g. "1.2.0 with the new export")
work.release.prompt:
Prepare a release of {name}: {text}

Raise the version wherever it is written, write the CHANGELOG entry from the commits since the last tag, check build and tests and commit it. Push and tag only if you may — else ask for approval and give the exact commands.
work.ask.hint: Learn something about the code — read only
work.ask.ph: What do you want to know about {name}?
work.ask.prompt:
Question about {name}: {text}

Look in the code and answer precisely, with files and lines. Change nothing.
cmd.hint: run without AI in the project folder
cmd.newPh: Own command, e.g. npm run e2e
cmd.fixPrompt:
The command `{c}` ends with code {code}. The end of its output:
```
{out}
```
Find the cause and fix it; then run the command again (if you may run it) until it passes.
chg.review.title: Review of the changes in {name}
chg.review.prompt: Review the changes in {name} that are not committed yet (git diff HEAD and new files). Change nothing. Name real bugs first — with file and line, why and how to fix —, then small things. Say at the end whether it can be committed like this.
chg.commit.title: Commit the changes in {name}
chg.commit.prompt: Commit the open changes in {name}: look at them (git status, git diff), group what belongs together into sensible commits with clear messages in the style of the earlier commits. Leave out files that don't belong in the repository (build folders, secrets). Don't push.
chg.push.title: Push {name}
chg.push.prompt: Push the commits of {name} that are not on the remote yet (git push). No force push. Say afterwards what was pushed.
app.title: New app with AI
app.hint: Claude makes the app in a new folder, with a skeleton, README and first tests — then you build it further step by step in the project.
app.name: Name
app.parentHint: A new folder for the app is made in this folder.
app.whatPh: Describe the app in your own words: what for, for whom, the main features. Claude builds a small version that runs first.
app.git: Make a git repository with a first commit
app.foot: Claude works in the new folder in auto mode; pushing and publishing stay with you.
app.needWhat: Describe briefly what the app should do.
app.promptGit: Make a git repository (git init, a fitting .gitignore) and commit the first version.
app.kind.studio.desc: Like the other Studio apps: Tauri 2, Rust and HTML/JS without a framework
app.kind.studio.spec: a desktop app like the Studio apps: Tauri 2 (Rust) with a UI of plain HTML/CSS/JS without a framework in ui/, texts in src-tauri/i18n/de.json and en.json, Rust tests with cargo test
app.kind.web.desc: HTML, CSS and JavaScript — runs in the browser
app.kind.web.spec: a web app of HTML, CSS and JavaScript that runs in the browser without a build (open index.html)
app.kind.tauri.desc: Tauri 2 with a web framework of your choice
app.kind.tauri.spec: a desktop app with Tauri 2; choose what fits best for the UI and explain why in the README
app.kind.rust.desc: A command-line program or a library in Rust
app.kind.rust.spec: a Rust program (cargo), with tests (cargo test)
app.kind.python.desc: A script or program in Python, with pytest
app.kind.python.spec: a Python program with pyproject.toml and tests with pytest
app.kind.free.desc: Claude picks the fitting technology and says why
app.kind.free.spec: choose the technology that fits this app best and explain the choice in the README
rt.projectHint: The routine works in the project's folders and with its rights.
rt.noProjectHint: Without a project you give folders and rights below yourself.
todo.noProject: This list belongs to no project.
todo.tickHint: Agent Studio ticks an item when Claude has done it
tpl.review.desc: Reviews the day's changes in the evening and reports bugs without changing anything.
tpl.review.prompt: Review today's changes in this project (the commits since yesterday and what is not committed yet). Change nothing. Name real bugs with file and line, the most important first; if all looks good, say so briefly.
